newsitem.title: GERMANY: Lufthansa confirms May 14 alliance briefing.
newsitem.headline: Lufthansa confirms May 14 alliance briefing.

text.p: German airline Deutsche Lufthansa AG on Friday confirmed it would release on May 14 its plans for cooperation with its four main airline partners.

"I can confirm that there will be a briefing on May 14," a Lufthansa spokesman said in response to enquiries, adding that the airline would discuss plans to expand its existing relationships with other major airlines.

But he would not confirm a report in the Frankfurter Allgemeine Zeitung newspaper on Friday that it would unveil an alliance with partners Thai Airways, United Airlines, Scandinavian Airlines and Air Canada under the name "Star Alliance".
"I cannot give any more details because they have not been definitely decided yet," the spokesman said.
There has been unconfirmed speculation that Lufthansa and its partners were due to open their cooperation to up to five other airlines, creating the largest alliance in the industry.
Aside from the existing five collaborators, industry talk has put forward Brazil's Varig, All-Nippon Airways, South African Airways and British Midland.
SAS said on Thursday that in the long-term "the doors (were) not closed for enlargement of the alliance" but did not confirm which airlines had been involved in any talks held so far.
Lufthansa and its existing partners are thought to be working on arrangements to link up their respective services yet --Mark John, Frankfurt Newsroom, +49 69 756525
